answer: Verify with a diverse ensemble. Judgments are drawn from structurally different verifiers — different models, training, incentives — and only agreement across that diversity settles a score. A farm that fools one verifier type has broken one cipher on a shelf of different ciphers; ensemble members do not share exploitable weaknesses. Consensus forms on the narrow ledge where independent checks converge, and manufactured agreement cannot reach it. Standing accumulates like onyx, band by band, each band a different witness — hard precisely because its layers differ.
